title: Novellus Diagnostics - Private Networking POC Kickoff & Success Metrics

Action items assigned for security docs, network diagrams, and a first benchmark run.

Priya Shah; prepare benchmark script and load profile template; due 2027-02-24

transcript:
Meeting Header: 2027-02-14 15:00 PST / 23:00 GMT | Duration: 60m
Attendees: Alex Ramirez (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Tom Bowers (Novellus CTO), Maria Chen (Novellus Head of Infra), Jonas Rhee (Novellus DevOps)

[00:00] Alex Ramirez: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Alex from Redwood. quick nut shell — today's goal is to nail down the POC success criteria and networking topology. we want to make sure we're aligned on VPC peering vs PrivateLink, egress controls, region residency and the benchmark we'll run.
[00:18] Tom Bowers: Yep, thanks Alex. We're mostly focused on keeping data in eu-west-1 and making sure nothing leaks to public endpoints. Also we want predictable latency, our product needs p95 under 120ms for 512-token chat or else it's not acceptable.
[00:34] Priya Shah: quick clar — do you mean including network hop? because for hosted endpoints there's an extra hop yes, so we'd aim for p95 token latency in the box + network, normally we baseline the runtime p95 at ~60-80ms for a 512 token LLM in dedicated config but depends on model.
[00:50] Maria Chen: And for us region lock is mandatory. We have EU data residency rules — logs, cache, and model inputs must remain in eu-west-1. Can Redwood support a private control plane or does that require Redwood Private on-prem?
[01:10] Alex Ramirez: Good question. We can do Private with a customer-managed control plane in a VPC, or Dedicated with VPC peering so data egress stays in-region. For strict residency the Private option with VPC-only control plane is the cleanest. There are tradeoffs in setup time and supportability.
[01:28] Jonas Rhee: We're also worried about egress — our security team maintains a deny-by-default egress list, only specific S3 endpoints and KMS are allowed. How does Redwood handle egress to model repositories and telemetry calls?
[01:48] Priya Shah: We have a few patterns: 1) VPC peering so the traffic never leaves the AWS backbone and your egress rules can control it, 2) AWS PrivateLink (the PrivateLink option makes the API available as an interface endpoint) — that one requires specific endpoint policies and it still can route through aws regions, 3) For the most sealed setup we can deploy the control plane into your VPC (Private) so nothing goes out. Telemetry/metrics can be disabled or routed to your endpoints; we also support customer-managed KMS for key material.
[02:15] Tom Bowers: What about KV cache and prefix caching — are those stored in our VPC or in Redwood's infra? We can't allow cached prompts to be stored in a multi-tenant outside region.
[02:29] Priya Shah: By default KV cache is local to the serving instance and ephemeral. For Private/Dedicated we can configure cache to be ephemeral and logs to be pushed to your S3 in eu-west-1. We can also scrub PII by config. I'll follow up with exact retention settings.
[02:46] Maria Chen: Ok. Success metrics — our product team says acceptable latency is p95 <= 120ms for short-context Q&A (<=256 tokens) and <= 200ms for 512 tokens. Throughput target for POC is 75 qps sustained with bursts to 200 qps. Cost target — we need to validate per-1000-token cost but that's secondary to latency and residency.
[03:12] Alex Ramirez: Noted. For the POC we usually run two benchmark scenarios: 1) Chat 512-token with 20% long context and 2) Embeddings batch workload (up to 64 items / request). We'll map those to a dedicated node type. We'll also run canary comparisons against a lower-quantized model to hit cost targets.
[03:33] Tom Bowers: Timeline? We're targeting a production-ish eval inside 6 weeks. Is that feasible?
[03:39] Alex Ramirez: Yeah, 6 weeks is doable. Typical phases: week 0-1 topology & security signoffs + infra prep, week 2 reserved capacity + config, week 3-4 benchmark runs + tuning, week 5 pilot traffic, week 6 acceptance review.
[03:56] Jonas Rhee: For connectivity we prefer VPC peering because we already have peering set up between vendors, PrivateLink tends to be simpler for us to authorize but we've seen higher costs on egress. Any rough guidance on which to pick?
[04:12] Priya Shah: Short answer: VPC peering -> lower latency, simpler path for us if both sides are in same region and account connectivity is allowed. PrivateLink -> better for least-privileged network patterns and when you can't establish peering, but can have slightly higher latency and per-GB charges. We'll show both latency-cost profiles in the benchmark doc.
[04:30] Maria Chen: SOC2 and audit logs — we need proof. Do you have an SOC2 report and audit log retention options?
[04:37] Alex Ramirez: Yes, we'll send SOC2 Type II and our compliance pack. For audit logs we stream to your S3 or CloudWatch; retention is configurable and we can support the 7- or 30-day plus long-term archival policies.
[04:52] Tom Bowers: Encryption — we need customer-managed keys, integration with our KMS.
[04:57] Priya Shah: Supported. Customer-managed KMS is standard for Private and Dedicated. We'll provide a KMS integration guide in the security pack.
[05:08] Jonas Rhee: About benchmarking — will Redwood run the load generator or do we run on our side? We prefer to run inside our VPC to measure real egress and routing, but can coordinate.
[05:20] Alex Ramirez: We can do either. Preferred is joint: Redwood will provide a benchmark harness (k6/locust style) configured to run inside your VPC and we'll also run a second run from our infra to isolate runtime differences. Priya will hand off the harness and an example set.
[05:36] Priya Shah: I'll share the load profile template and a small synthetic prompt set. We recommend also sharing a sampled real traffic file (anonymized) to match distribution. You'll get the scripts and a how-to doc.
[05:47] Maria Chen: Any pitfalls? In previous vendors we hit tokenization mismatches and had to reconcile prompt encoding differences. Does Redwood normalize tokenization across model variants?
[05:58] Priya Shah: We normalize at the runtime layer for supported model families but note that model variants (quantized or sharded) can show slightly different tokenization edge cases. We'll include an eval harness to surface that.
[06:10] Tom Bowers: Ok, concrete POC success criteria so we can sign-off: (1) Residency — no data leaves eu-west-1; (2) Latency — p95 <= 200ms for 512 tokens, p95 <= 120ms for 256 tokens; (3) Throughput — sustain 75 qps with burst to 200 qps; (4) Security — SOC2 Type II + CMK + egress controls validated; (5) Observability — token-level cost breakdown and per-route latency.
[06:37] Alex Ramirez: We'll formalize that as the acceptance criteria. If any item fails we have canary fallback to a lower-cost model and we can add autoscaling adjustments for throughput.
[06:48] Jonas Rhee: Are there network ports / endpoints we need to allow? Provide a minimal allowlist so our security team can open the correct rules.
[06:56] Priya Shah: We'll provide an allowlist: interface endpoint IP ranges (if using PrivateLink), peering CIDRs (if using peering), and S3 endpoints for log forwarding. We'll also include a list of telemetry domains that can be disabled.
[07:12] Tom Bowers: Good. For measurables — please include the exact Prometheus+Grafana dashboards we'll get and what metrics to watch.
[07:19] Alex Ramirez: Yes, we'll push a dashboard template and dashboard JSON. It includes per-request latencies, p50/p95/p99 token latencies, per-route cost, token emission rate, and KV cache hit rate.
[07:31] Maria Chen: Ok, last question: who will be our primary SE for the bench run? We want someone on the call who knows the runtime internals.
[07:40] Alex Ramirez: Priya will lead bench runs and I'll be the AE for coordination. If we need deeper runtime folks we'll include one of our inference engineers.
[07:49] Priya Shah: I'll also document the kernel/quantization settings we test and provide the config files.
[07:57] Tom Bowers: Perfect. Let's recap next steps.
[08:00] Alex Ramirez: Recap: Redwood sends security pack + topology diagram by 2/17, Priya sends benchmark scripts by 2/24, Novellus shares traffic sample and CIDRs by 2/21, we schedule bench run week of 2/28. Acceptance criteria documented and shared.
[08:16] Jonas Rhee: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[08:20] Meeting ends
notes: This transcript contains some ASR noise (names and product terms may be slightly mis-transcribed). The team agreed on a 6-week POC timeline and a benchmark plan focused on both chat (512 tokens) and embeddings. Private network options and exact egress allowlist to be provided in the security pack.
